data.body:
Implemented as Gerrit 2232, in the report-not-fail shape argued above.

- /health now returns {"in_flight": N, "store": {"path", "present", "expected"}} and still
  200s. store_status() never raises: a probe that can throw would turn a store-resolution
  problem into a restart loop under `restart: always`, which is the opposite of reporting it.
- autodeploy readiness gate refuses to promote on `expected AND NOT present`, with a named
  mcp-store-missing error. Gated on expected, NOT presence alone — that is the property that
  makes this safe to land while the box still has no store. An older container whose /health
  predates the field reports neither key and is treated as not-expected, so a mixed-version
  deploy cannot be blocked by it.
- mcp_server boot emits one WARNING naming the store path when absent (AC2). The
  log-and-continue posture is kept; it just says something now.

IMPLEMENTATION NARROWING: `expected` reads the REBAR_TRACKER_DIR env override alone, not the
parsed config. The repo's check_config_ownership gate reserves load_config to approved seams,
and coupling a health probe to config parsing is a bad idea independently. A project that
instead declares a non-default tracker.dir in config reports expected=False and simply does not
get the strict gate — it degrades to the old behaviour rather than misreporting. The deployment
surface that matters here sets the env var explicitly.

Mutation-checked: hard-coding `expected` to True — the exact mistake that would cause the
outage this shape avoids — turns test_no_configured_dir_is_not_expected RED.
